How can I change a ceramic product photo to a three-quarter view while preserving its shape and material? Search the web and cite the sources supporting your answer.
To change a ceramic product photo to a three-quarter view while preserving its shape and material, you can use specialized digital editing workflows or modern AI-driven product visualization tools.
Depending on your technical comfort level and the assets you have, choose one of the options below:
Option 1: Advanced Perspective Warping (Best for exact material preservation)
If you want to keep the exact original photo texturing and glazes intact, you can use professional desktop software like Adobe Photoshop or free alternatives like Photopea.
Convert to a Smart Object: Open your image in Photoshop, duplicate your layer, and go to Filter > Convert for Smart Filters to protect your original image quality. 
TikTok
·piximperfects
Apply Perspective Warp: Go to Edit > Perspective Warp. Click and drag to create grids (planes) over the faces of your ceramic object. For a three-quarter view, you will want to define the front and side planes so they snap together. 
TikTok
·piximperfects
Manipulate into Position: Switch the tool from "Layout" to "Warp" mode at the top. Drag the corners to adjust the perspective to a three-quarter angle. Hold Shift while clicking lines if you need to keep certain edges straight.
Note: If you don't own Photoshop, Photopea offers a similar, free web-based option using Edit > Free Transform > Distort to manipulate individual corner points. 
YouTube
·Learn Canva with Greg
 +1
Option 2: Image-to-3D AI Generation (Best for seamless rotation)
If your initial photo is purely flat (e.g., straight-on) and lacks the side data needed for warping, you can use modern AI commerce tools to re-render the product.
Upload to an AI Product Generator: Use generative ecommerce platforms (such as Freepik, Kling, or specialized product photography tools). 
Instagram
·Safwaan Mujawar
 +1
Structure the Prompt: Use highly targeted, structure-preserving prompts. For example: "Change the perspective of the ceramic item to a three-quarter studio view, maintain absolute product consistency, shape, material glaze, and 4:5 aspect ratio". 
Instagram
·Safwaan Mujawar
Use 3D Reference Conversions: Many AI tools feature a "Turn Image into 360-degree View" option where you upload the reference image, input a prompt specifying the new angle, and the engine generates a multi-angle view or brief video showing the object from a three-quarter perspective. 
YouTube
·DolphyAI
Option 3: Manual Reshooting (Best for flawless professional results)
If digital manipulation distorts the unique glaze highlights or complex curves of your ceramic piece, the most reliable method is to physically reshoot it.
Set up a neutral backdrop (like a white foam board) using soft, natural sunlight to ensure your colors remain completely accurate.
Place the piece on a tripod-aligned setup and physically rotate the ceramic item 45 degrees away from the camera to capture a true three-quarter angle.
